intro: Florida runs its elections through an elected Supervisor of Elections in each county, who keeps the voter rolls, mails ballots, and sets early-voting sites.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and school board offices, many city and town elections, and any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: 29 days before the election. You can still update an existing registration after this date.

src.label: Florida Division of Elections — election dates

dates.label: Vote-by-mail request due by 5 pm
dates.detail: Ask your county Supervisor of Elections in person, by mail, email, fax, or phone. A request covers one election cycle, so make sure yours is on file for 2026 even if you voted by mail before.

dates.label: Early voting — the statewide minimum
dates.detail: Every county holds early voting at least these days. Many counties add more days, from as early as Oct. 19 — check your county below.

src.label: Florida Division of Elections — early voting
Florida Division of Elections — election dates

dates.label: Election Day — and mail ballots must arrive
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm, and on Election Day you vote at your assigned precinct. A mail ballot must reach your Supervisor of Elections by 7 pm — a postmark is not enough.

src.label: Florida Division of Elections — Election Day voting

id_rule.text: Bring a current photo ID that also shows your signature — a Florida driver's license or ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, or a debit or credit card with your photo, among others. If your photo ID has no signature, bring a second ID that does. Without ID you can still vote a provisional ballot.

src.label: Florida Division of Elections — Election Day voting

check.text: Polling place, sample ballot, and mail ballot status come from your county Supervisor of Elections (below).

filings.name: Form 1 — Statement of Financial Interests
filings.who: Elected city and town officials, and candidates for those offices.
filings.where: Filed online with the Florida Commission on Ethics; public and searchable at disclosure.floridaethics.gov.
filings.when: Each year by July 1; candidates file when they qualify. A 2023 law moved elected town officials to the fuller Form 6, but a federal court has blocked enforcing that while a lawsuit goes on.
